subject.title: Track OpenClaw seams needed for full imported-plugin parity

question: Which source-neutral public host contracts should OpenClaw expose, and what authorization, lifecycle, validation, and compatibility guarantees must each contract enforce before Babelfish may consume it?
rationale: The correct API shape determines durable approval authority, connector authentication, agent isolation, and ownership of existing bundle infrastructure; automation cannot safely choose those security and product contracts.

options.title: Approve staged host contracts
options.body: Define and security-review narrow public contracts individually, prioritizing approval, connector, and agent boundaries before adding Babelfish mappings.

options.title: Expose bundle projections first
options.body: Publicize only the existing bundle settings and LSP projection mechanisms while deferring new runtime and authentication APIs.

options.title: Keep gaps unsupported
options.body: Continue surfacing unsupported imports without approximation until OpenClaw has a broader plugin-host API strategy.

recommendation.title: Approve staged host contracts
recommendation.body: Define and security-review narrow public contracts individually, prioritizing approval, connector, and agent boundaries before adding Babelfish mappings.

likelyOwner.reason: The member-authored tracker demonstrates the clearest available ownership of the cross-repository parity requirements and their security constraints.
